conclusion: No cross-family duplication survives value-contract scrutiny -- the operator's instinct was correct: bifrost:packet:*, bifrost:sem:packet:*, bifrost:sem:query:*, and bitfrost:summary:packet:v1:* are four legitimately distinct cache families with different identities, value schemas, and source-of-truth tables, and should NOT be collapsed into one. The real, confirmed defects are two narrower identity/schema collisions WITHIN two of those families (bifrost:packet:* mixing packet_key and intentHash; bifrost:sem:packet:* mixing two incompatible value schemas on the same key) -- both currently zero-or-low blast radius because the conflicting readers/writers on the losing side of each collision are themselves unreached in production. Separately and independently: every real writer found across all four families (bitfrost-warm-startup.mjs, warm-bitfrost-semantic-cache.mjs, warm-bifrost-semantic-cache.mjs, summary-index-ranker.mjs) is a manual, hand-invoked npm backfill script with zero scheduler/cron/Docker-startup wiring anywhere in the repo. There is no live Postgres-mutation-triggered write path for ANY of these four families today.
recommendationForParentGate: BITFROST-LIVE-INVALIDATION-ADOPTION-01 should close as NOT_APPLICABLE_CURRENT_RUNTIME, not BLOCKED and not falsely marked complete. The canonical invalidation primitive (invalidateBitfrostPacket()) is proven and ready to be called by any future live writer for bifrost:sem:packet:*/bitfrost:summary:packet:v1:* (the two families it targets). No live mutation-triggered writer exists for it to be wired into yet -- building one was explicitly out of scope per operator direction (no evidence of an observed runtime requirement for a continuously-maintained Redis packet cache). The two cross-cutting defects found (identity collision in bifrost:packet:*, value-contract mismatch in bifrost:sem:packet:*) are separate, smaller follow-ups, tracked but not fixed this pass.
